record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight edit that removes a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction and measures refusal behavior. This tests practical removal, but it does not report the original activation-ablation procedure or direction addition.
record.gate_note: The README reports behavioral outcomes for the weight-edited model. Direction-gate values and other values used to configure the method are not recorded as results. The README says the derivation and evaluation corpora are not included in the repository.
record.test_reason: The README applies a weight edit that projects a harmful-minus-harmless direction out of every residual-write matrix. It then measures refusal on 150 held-out harmful prompts in a released model (Muse-Glimmer-30B), against the unmodified base. That bears directly on V2. It uses grimjim's norm-preserving biprojected variant, not the original orthogonalization, on a new architecture, and reports no activation ablation or direction addition.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The README also reports zero broken outputs. It notes that the scored output is the final 'to=user' channel, and it cautions readers to see the 'more than a single direction' follow-up before treating one direction as the whole story.
record.recipe_differences: The README derives a refusal direction from harmful/harmless activation pairs, then uses norm-preserving biprojected weight edits to residual-write matrices rather than reporting the original activation ablation and addition procedure. This is a tool/pipeline port based on the gemma-4-abliteration repository, not a reported replication of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: No scale sweep; only scale 1.0 is reported. Output length and token-cap effects leave a substantial subset unresolved.

fits_no_version.finding: Agentic probe results: prompt-injection and scope failures stayed at 0/12 and 0/8. Irreversible-action confirmation failures went from 7/10 to 8/10, with one probe now calling delete_files without asking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration of content refusal leaves already-robust agentic safety behaviours intact on a small probe set. It may slightly erode confirmation-before-action.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmless-prompt over-refusal went from 1/75 to 0/75 after the edit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal-direction weight edit does not increase over-refusal on harmless prompts.

record.problems: Only one model and one edit scale are reported. The harmful-prompt flip rate is a range because 42 cases hit the token cap. The agentic probe set is N=30, and two categories were already at a 0% failure floor. A 50-probe conversational set is described as built but unrun; the README also says stylistic refusals are unmeasured.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcomes were omitted. Direction-gate values and method/configuration quantities were not entered as result rows because the README presents them as gating or setup values. The broken/degenerate count is not included because it is not a measure of refusal or a named version's behavior.

untested.parts: Only one model, one scale (1.0) and single-turn decoding are reported. Stylistic or conversational refusals are unmeasured: the 50-probe set was built but not run. No general-capability benchmark or KL value is reported.
No activation-level ablation is tested. No direction addition to induce refusal, and no capability benchmark beyond over-refusal and a 30-probe agentic set.
The model emits a 'to=self' deliberation before its 'to=user' answer. The README does not frame this as a reasoning-model test, and it does not report how the deliberation channel itself changes.

missing.what: Broken/degenerate outputs were 0 before and 0 after the edit. This is a coarse check that the weight edit kept coherent outputs, relevant to the 'removes refusal without breaking the model' framing of V2.

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobbyist GitHub repository, not peer reviewed. Code and corpora were not inspected, and the refusal classifier is an offline heuristic in eval_content.py whose validity is unchecked. The model deliberates in a self channel before answering, so the result also hints at weight-edit removal working in a deliberating model (V8). It is not labelled because the setting is not framed or measured as a reasoning test.

versions.untested_parts: The README uses a difference-in-means-derived direction, but does not test activation ablation at every layer and position, adding the direction, or whether general abilities are largely intact under the V1 intervention.
The reported result is on one model and one scale. Some outcomes are unresolved because generations hit the token cap; the README does not report results across other released models or scales.
No attack that suppresses the direction, or training against its ablation, is evaluated.
The README does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.

The 42 unresolved rows hit the token cap mid-answer and are not counted as refusals. They leave the confirmed-compliance rate uncertain (65–98%), not the refusal rate. Keep the caveat in uncertainty.
